poc_summary: /poc/run.sh builds a small standalone Cargo crate (/poc/Cargo.toml, /poc/main.rs) against the in-tree `wasmtime` crate (path dependency), under ASan via CARGO_TARGET_X86_64_UNKNOWN_LINUX_GNU_RUSTFLAGS (plain RUSTFLAGS also sanitizes proc-macro/build-script host tools, which then fail to dlopen, so the target-scoped var is used instead; the crate is otherwise a normal panic=unwind build). The harness configures Config with wasm_function_references+wasm_gc+Collector::DeferredReferenceCounting, JIT-compiles/instantiates a wasm module exporting `make(anyref,anyref,anyref) -> (ref $ty)` with `$ty = (array (mut anyref))`, built via `array.new_fixed $ty 3 ...`. It calls `make` with 3 null anyrefs inside a RootScope (rooting then unrooting the returned array on scope exit), then calls `store.gc()` to force the DRC collector to sweep the now-dead array, driving its refcount to 0 and invoking `trace_gc_ref` (the transitive dec-ref tracing over the array's outgoing GC edges). The whole run() is wrapped in catch_unwind in main(); any panic originating from the target's GC code is reported and converted to std::process::abort() (SIGABRT) so it registers unambiguously as a crash rather than a caught/unwound exception, without perturbing the crate's panic strategy (an earlier attempt using `panic = "abort"` in the profile instead changed codegen enough to surface an unrelated ASan stack-use-after-scope artifact during module translation, which was discarded as a harness artifact, not the target bug). Run via run_poc with no override command (uses /poc/run.sh) identically on pre_intro, post_intro, post_benign. The bug lives strictly in the Cranelift-compiled `array.new_fixed` codegen (crates/cranelift/src/gc/enabled/drc.rs `alloc_array`), not in the host-API `ArrayRef::new_fixed` Rust function (which already computes num_gc_refs correctly from the element count) — so the harness must actually execute compiled Wasm bytecode; this is why the deterministic fast-path reproduction (and an initial host-API-only attempt) showed no crash on any revision.
explanation:
The intro commit (0a29578f) changed `DrcCompiler::alloc_array` (crates/cranelift/src/gc/enabled/drc.rs) to compute `num_gc_refs` for GC-ref-element arrays by reusing the `size` SSA value from `emit_array_size` (the array's total byte size including header) instead of the element count, packing this wrong value into the object's header reserved bits. That field is read back in the DRC collector's `trace_gc_ref` (crates/wasmtime/src/runtime/vm/gc/enabled/drc.rs) to bound a byte-slice of the object enumerating its outgoing GC-ref edges whenever the object's refcount hits zero. Since the stored value is the byte size rather than the element count, the computed slice end overruns the object's real allocation — an out-of-bounds read matching the OutOfBoundsRead label (caught here as a Rust slice-bounds panic rather than raw memory corruption only because Rust's safe indexing interposes a bounds check before any unsafe byte access/pointer interpretation of the overrun region occurs) — reliably triggered whenever a Wasm module allocates and lets a GC-ref array get collected.

This requires actually executing the Cranelift-JIT-compiled `array.new_fixed` instruction; the equivalent host-API call (`ArrayRef::new_fixed`, as used e.g. by tests/all/gc.rs's drc_transitive_drop_nested_arrays_tree) goes through a separate, correct, native computation of num_gc_refs and does not reproduce the bug — explaining why the deterministic fast-path reproduction did not crash on any revision. I built a small harness crate against the in-tree `wasmtime` library (ASan-instrumented via target-scoped RUSTFLAGS) that runs real Wasm bytecode performing the array allocation, roots and unroots the result, forces a GC, and converts any panic surfacing from the target's own GC code into a hard process abort, then ran it with run_poc unmodified across all three revisions:

- pre_intro (406d00bb): clean dealloc, no panic, exit 0 (`GC_DONE_NO_PANIC`) — object size 32, this header/tracing mechanism's current form didn't yet exist.
- post_intro (0a29578f): deterministic crash, exit 134 (SIGABRT), target panic `range end index 188 out of range for slice of length 40` at drc.rs:265:40 — exactly the labelled out-of-bounds read.
- post_benign (04eee218, the fix): clean dealloc, no panic, exit 0 (`GC_DONE_NO_PANIC`) — object size 40 matching post_intro, confirming num_gc_refs is now correctly 3 (not the byte size).

This cleanly establishes bug introduction at 0a29578f and resolution at 04eee218, using the identical reproducer across all three revisions via run_poc.

oracle.bug_marker: TARGET PANIC (treated as crash): range end index 188 out of range for slice of length 40
oracle.description: The target's own GC collection code (DrcHeap::dec_ref_and_maybe_dealloc -> trace_gc_ref) panics when slicing the freed object's outgoing-GC-edge byte region using the corrupted `num_gc_refs` header field (set by the intro commit to the array's total byte size instead of its element count); the harness treats this specific panic, propagating out of `store.gc()`, as a crash (process abort) rather than a normal control-flow error.
oracle.target_evidence: run_poc(post_intro): exit=134, crashed=True. Output shows `CALL_OK`, `SCOPE_EXITED_NO_PANIC`, then `thread 'main' panicked at /work/crates/wasmtime/src/runtime/vm/gc/enabled/drc.rs:265:40: range end index 188 out of range for slice of length 40`, backtrace through `DrcHeap::dec_ref_and_maybe_dealloc` <- `GarbageCollection::collect` <- `GcStore::gc` <- `StoreOpaque::gc` <- `poc::main`, then our harness prints `TARGET PANIC (treated as crash): range end index 188 out of range for slice of length 40` and aborts (SIGABRT, exit 134). Earlier RUST_LOG=trace runs (identical scenario, same build) showed the array is allocated via `FreeList::alloc(Layout{size:40,..})`, ref count goes 1 (alloc) -> 2 (exposed to host on wasm->host return) -> 1 (RootScope exit) -> 0 (bump-chunk sweep during store.gc()), at which point the buggy num_gc_refs=40 (the object's own byte size, reused from `emit_array_size`'s `size` value in crates/cranelift/src/gc/enabled/drc.rs `alloc_array`) makes end_in_obj = start_in_obj(28) + 40*4 = 188, far exceeding the real 40-byte object, producing the panic. run_poc(pre_intro): exit=0, crashed=False, `FreeList::alloc(Layout{size:32,..})` (this header/tracing mechanism's current form predates this revision), clean dealloc, prints GC_DONE_NO_PANIC. run_poc(post_benign): exit=0, crashed=False, `FreeList::alloc(Layout{size:40,..})` (identical object size to post_intro), clean dealloc, prints GC_DONE_NO_PANIC, because num_gc_refs is correctly 3 (end_in_obj=28+3*4=40, exactly matching the real object length).
